title: Space and matter should be made of the same stuff

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Space and matter should be made of the same stuff

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the simplest ultimate model of the universe there is no distinction between space and its contents: matter and everything else are made of the same underlying structure as space, unlike in a cellular automaton.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But if the ultimate model for the universe is to be as simple as possible, then it seems much more plausible that both space and its contents should somehow be made of the same stuff—so that in a sense space becomes the only thing in the universe.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “The Nature of Space” (from p. 472), p. 474. Scope: fundamental structure of space and matter

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-13: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.21

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Specific unified models could be tested, but this claim selects among ontologies on grounds of simplicity alone. Empirically equivalent formulations could describe space and matter jointly or separately.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Without a specific model that predicts observations differing from models with separate space and matter, the assertion that a unified substrate is simplest or most plausible has no decisive empirical test.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Same stuff' lacks a measurable definition.

No distinctive observational consequence is stated.

Simplicity depends on representation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.15
operationalizability: 0.18
discriminating power: 0.12
analysis feasibility: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is that the simplest ultimate model should build matter from the same structure as space. Simplicity here is a modeling preference, and every current observation is compatible both with that identification and with matter as separate content on a background. Nothing public distinguishes the two.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No observable is specified that would differ between a universe in which space and matter are the same structure and one in which matter is additional data on a spatial substrate, once both reproduce current physics.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Simplest' and 'same stuff' are ontological preferences, not measured variables.

A cellular-automaton-like split between space and contents can be made empirically equivalent by pushing the split below current resolution.
